title: Acute Myeloid Leukemia
summary: TARGET AML is the reference paediatric AML cohort. RNA sequencing covers 2,281 cases and microRNA 1,836, with smaller whole genome, exome, methylation and targeted panel layers. 251 patients are recorded as Black or African American, one of the larger absolute numbers in any cohort here, and vital status is informative for 86.6% with a usable overall survival endpoint.
one_liner: 2,492 children and young adults with acute myeloid leukaemia - the largest paediatric cancer genomics cohort in this corpus, with 3.5 years of median follow-up and therapeutic agents recorded for 35% of cases.

useful_for.question: How does the genomic landscape of paediatric AML differ from adult AML?
useful_for.rationale: 2,281 RNA-sequenced paediatric cases can be contrasted directly with adult AML cohorts, and the marker paper established that the differences are substantial and age-dependent. This remains the definitive paediatric comparison set.
useful_for.statistical_note: Adult comparison cohorts differ in platform and processing; model batch explicitly.

evidence.note: Written by a named reviewer after reading the source documentation and the measured field coverage. Not machine-generated.

useful_for.question: Which molecular features predict survival in paediatric AML?
useful_for.rationale: Vital status informative for 86.6% of 2,492 cases with median follow-up of 41.7 months gives a well-powered survival cohort, and therapeutic agents are recorded for 35% so treatment can be partially controlled.
useful_for.statistical_note: Cause of death is not recorded, so competing risks from treatment-related mortality cannot be separated from disease death.

useful_for.question: Are there racial differences in paediatric AML biology or outcome?
useful_for.rationale: 251 Black or African American patients alongside 1,551 white patients is one of the better-powered settings in this corpus for a race-stratified comparison in a paediatric cancer.
useful_for.statistical_note: Race is self-reported; genetic ancestry from germline data is the more defensible variable for biological claims. Treatment differences may confound outcome comparisons.

limitations.statement: Progression or recurrence is populated for 0.3% of cases and informative for none, and cause of death is absent entirely. Relapse - the central clinical event in paediatric AML - cannot be modeled from these records.
limitations.mitigation: Restrict to overall survival, or obtain relapse data from the trial group.

limitations.statement: Treatment type is populated for 86% of cases but therapeutic agents only for 35%, and treatment outcome detail is sparse. Protocol era spans many years with evolving therapy.
limitations.mitigation: Adjust for enrolment era; treat agent-level claims cautiously.
